brief_summary: Three-panel cross-section contrasting the MX leaf-crossing mechanism shared by the Durock T1, Boba U4T, Holy Panda X, and Gateron Lanes against two mechanisms that are not leaf-crossing at all: Topre's capacitive dome-collapse and the Alps SKCM Orange's internal slider snap. Establishes that leg geometry, not mechanism family, is the variable the rest of the article examines.
data_sources: apps/web/src/content/articles/durock-t1-deep-dive.mdx:'A Topre keypress is not a leaf crossing at all ... capacitive PCB pad reads the change in the spring's position as the actuation signal. There is no metal-on-metal contact anywhere in that stack.'

apps/web/src/content/articles/gateron-lanes-tactile-deep-dive.mdx:'a self-contained mechanism that generates its bump not through a leaf that a stem leg crosses, as every MX-compatible switch does, but through a resonant slider body that physically interrupts its own travel path'
apps/web/src/content/articles/topre-electrocapacitive-deep-dive.mdx:'a Topre keypress does not close a circuit at all'
